_comment: The per-cage wrapper Containerfile and the argv quoting baked into it, as `apple_container/wrapper.py` produces them.
why: the wrapper image is the cage's PID 1 and its argv is baked into it at build time. `_shlex_join_argv` is the whole defence against a `container.command` metacharacter reaching a shell, so both implementations have to agree on it byte for byte.

cases.containerfile:
FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04

# Many user images set a non-root USER (claude-code, codex, node:*) which
# would make the apt install step EACCES. cage-init runs as root until
# stage D's capsh-drop, so we don't lose the workload's uid-1000 invariant.
USER root

# Minimal install: route control, capsh, ping, trust store update. The
# apt/apk branches are best-effort; an image that doesn't have either
# package manager (distroless, etc.) just skips the install — the cage
# might still work if the binaries are already present in the base.
# Failure here surfaces as cage-init's "command not found" at boot time,
# which `container logs` shows clearly.
RUN if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
        apt-get update -qq \
        && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            iproute2 libcap2-bin iputils-ping ca-certificates iptables \
            dnsmasq-base \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* ; \
    elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
        apk add --no-cache iproute2 libcap iputils ca-certificates iptables dnsmasq ; \
    fi

# CTF F2 (0.22.6): the cage's /etc/resolv.conf defaulted to the apple-
# vmnet host gateway (.1) which does unrestricted recursion for any
# apex — a clean DNS-tunnel exfil channel. The egress sibling's dnsmasq
# is unreachable from the cage because macOS vmnet drops inter-microVM
# UDP (verified by reading apple/container source, see
# NonisolatedInterfaceStrategy.swift:32-56). The only fix is a local
# dnsmasq inside the cage VM scoped to the per-cage `domains.allow`.
# setcap so a non-root `acdns` user can bind :53; matches the egress
# image's pattern (Containerfile.egress:56-63). Best-effort because
# distroless / alpine bases may not have dnsmasq-base.
#
# acdns gets the same three-way user-creation fallback as the uid-1000
# step below, for the same reason and in the same order — see that
# comment. The dnsmasq guard does not make this step safe: the apk
# branch above *installs* dnsmasq, so `[ -x /usr/sbin/dnsmasq ]` passes
# on exactly the kind of base (Alpine) that has no shadow-utils, where
# the bare `useradd` this used to be aborted the build right here.
# The `acdns` GROUP is created explicitly on the adduser path because
# busybox's `-S` would otherwise file the user under `nogroup`, and
# cage-init.sh stage A' does `chown acdns:acdns /var/log/agentcage` so
# the dropped-priv dnsmasq can open the log-facility file the shared
# dnsmasq.conf names. That chown is `|| true`, so a missing group turns
# into dnsmasq failing to start, several stages later.
RUN if [ -x /usr/sbin/dnsmasq ]; then \
        setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /usr/sbin/dnsmasq \
        && (getent passwd acdns >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || grep -q '^acdns:' /etc/passwd \
            || if command -v useradd >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                   useradd --uid 201 --system --no-create-home \
                           --shell /usr/sbin/nologin --home-dir /var/empty acdns; \
               elif command -v adduser >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                   (getent group acdns >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    || grep -q '^acdns:' /etc/group \
                    || addgroup -g 201 -S acdns) \
                   && adduser -u 201 -G acdns -S -D -H -h /var/empty \
                              -s /usr/sbin/nologin acdns; \
               else \
                   printf 'acdns:x:201:201::/var/empty:/usr/sbin/nologin\n' >>/etc/passwd \
                   && printf 'acdns:x:201:\n' >>/etc/group; \
               fi) ; \
    fi

# Ensure a uid-1000 user exists for the cage workload. Bases like
# ubuntu (`ubuntu`), node (`node`), claude-code (`claude`) ship their
# own at uid 1000 — we reuse those. Only synthesize `cage` as a
# fallback when uid 1000 is truly free: useradd refuses to share a uid,
# which is why we don't try to alias the existing name to `cage`.
#
# Three creation paths, because `useradd` is shadow-utils and not POSIX
# — and a base without it is a *shipped scaffold*. `busybox` has
# neither `useradd` nor `getent`; against it the single unconditional
# `useradd --uid 1000 --create-home` this step used to be exited 127
# with "useradd: not found", so `--scaffold busybox` could not build at
# all on the backend macOS picks by default. Same tolerance for a
# minimal base that the apt/apk block above already states.
#
# Ordering is most-capable first and is load-bearing: shadow-utils
# `useradd` has to win on Debian/Ubuntu/node, because *their* `adduser`
# is Debian's perl wrapper, which shares the name with busybox's applet
# and none of its flags. busybox/Alpine `adduser` is second; its `-D`
# is mandatory, since without it adduser prompts for a password and the
# build hangs rather than failing. Appending to /etc/passwd and
# /etc/group is last, for a base that has a shell but neither tool.
#
# The "already taken?" probe can't be `getent` alone for the same
# reason: with no `getent` binary the lookup exits 127, and `! getent`
# reads a missing *tool* as a free uid. The grep over /etc/passwd is
# the fallback — inside a cage image the files source is the only NSS
# source there is.
#
# The home directory is not optional. cage-init.sh stage D re-exports
# HOME from field 6 of the uid-1000 entry and dies if it is empty, and
# anything the workload writes beneath it (claude-code's ~/.claude,
# npm's ~/.npm) is EACCES unless the uid owns it. So rather than
# assuming /home/cage, the tail reads field 6 back out of /etc/passwd —
# whichever branch wrote it — and makes that path exist and belong to
# 1000. No chmod: useradd and adduser each pick a sane mode, and
# forcing one here would widen a base whose login.defs chose 0750.
# An empty field 6 fails the RUN on purpose; none of the three branches
# can produce one, so it would mean /etc/passwd was not what we wrote.
RUN if ! getent passwd 1000 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && ! grep -q '^[^:]*:[^:]*:1000:' /etc/passwd; then \
        if command -v useradd >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
            useradd --uid 1000 --create-home --shell /bin/sh cage; \
        elif command -v adduser >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
            adduser -u 1000 -h /home/cage -s /bin/sh -D cage; \
        else \
            printf 'cage:x:1000:1000::/home/cage:/bin/sh\n' >>/etc/passwd \
            && printf 'cage:x:1000:\n' >>/etc/group; \
        fi \
        && cage_home=$(grep '^[^:]*:[^:]*:1000:' /etc/passwd | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f6) \
        && [ -n "${cage_home}" ] \
        && mkdir -p "${cage_home}" \
        && chown 1000:1000 "${cage_home}"; \
    fi

# Bake the user's original argv as a shell-escaped one-shot script.
# cage-init.sh exec's this after capsh-dropping. The shlex.quote on the
# Python side handles every metacharacter (spaces, $VAR, &&, ; etc.) so
# the resulting `exec ...` line is safe to feed straight to /bin/sh
# without further parsing. Closes the I2 argv-injection risk from the
# eng review on the prior runtime-jq approach.
RUN mkdir -p /opt/agentcage /etc/agentcage
RUN cat > /opt/agentcage/cage-cmd.sh <<'CAGECMD'
#!/bin/sh
exec sleep infinity
CAGECMD
RUN chmod 0755 /opt/agentcage/cage-cmd.sh

# cage-init.sh staged into the build context by stage_build_context
# (copies from src/agentcage/data/apple-container/cage-init.sh).
COPY cage-init.sh /opt/agentcage/cage-init.sh
RUN chmod 0755 /opt/agentcage/cage-init.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/agentcage/cage-init.sh"]
CMD []

# distroless / alpine bases may not have dnsmasq-base.
#
# acdns gets the same three-way user-creation fallback as the uid-1000
# step below, for the same reason and in the same order — see that
# comment. The dnsmasq guard does not make this step safe: the apk
# branch above *installs* dnsmasq, so `[ -x /usr/sbin/dnsmasq ]` passes
# on exactly the kind of base (Alpine) that has no shadow-utils, where
# the bare `useradd` this used to be aborted the build right here.
# The `acdns` GROUP is created explicitly on the adduser path because
# busybox's `-S` would otherwise file the user under `nogroup`, and
# cage-init.sh stage A' does `chown acdns:acdns /var/log/agentcage` so
# the dropped-priv dnsmasq can open the log-facility file the shared
# dnsmasq.conf names. That chown is `|| true`, so a missing group turns
# into dnsmasq failing to start, several stages later.
RUN if [ -x /usr/sbin/dnsmasq ]; then \
        setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /usr/sbin/dnsmasq \
        && (getent passwd acdns >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || grep -q '^acdns:' /etc/passwd \
            || if command -v useradd >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                   useradd --uid 201 --system --no-create-home \
                           --shell /usr/sbin/nologin --home-dir /var/empty acdns; \
               elif command -v adduser >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                   (getent group acdns >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    || grep -q '^acdns:' /etc/group \
                    || addgroup -g 201 -S acdns) \
                   && adduser -u 201 -G acdns -S -D -H -h /var/empty \
                              -s /usr/sbin/nologin acdns; \
               else \
                   printf 'acdns:x:201:201::/var/empty:/usr/sbin/nologin\n' >>/etc/passwd \
                   && printf 'acdns:x:201:\n' >>/etc/group; \
               fi) ; \
    fi

# Ensure a uid-1000 user exists for the cage workload. Bases like
# ubuntu (`ubuntu`), node (`node`), claude-code (`claude`) ship their
# own at uid 1000 — we reuse those. Only synthesize `cage` as a
# fallback when uid 1000 is truly free: useradd refuses to share a uid,
# which is why we don't try to alias the existing name to `cage`.
#
# Three creation paths, because `useradd` is shadow-utils and not POSIX
# — and a base without it is a *shipped scaffold*. `busybox` has
# neither `useradd` nor `getent`; against it the single unconditional
# `useradd --uid 1000 --create-home` this step used to be exited 127
# with "useradd: not found", so `--scaffold busybox` could not build at
# all on the backend macOS picks by default. Same tolerance for a
# minimal base that the apt/apk block above already states.
#
# Ordering is most-capable first and is load-bearing: shadow-utils
# `useradd` has to win on Debian/Ubuntu/node, because *their* `adduser`
# is Debian's perl wrapper, which shares the name with busybox's applet
# and none of its flags. busybox/Alpine `adduser` is second; its `-D`
# is mandatory, since without it adduser prompts for a password and the
# build hangs rather than failing. Appending to /etc/passwd and
# /etc/group is last, for a base that has a shell but neither tool.
#
# The "already taken?" probe can't be `getent` alone for the same
# reason: with no `getent` binary the lookup exits 127, and `! getent`
# reads a missing *tool* as a free uid. The grep over /etc/passwd is
# the fallback — inside a cage image the files source is the only NSS
# source there is.
#
# The home directory is not optional. cage-init.sh stage D re-exports
# HOME from field 6 of the uid-1000 entry and dies if it is empty, and
# anything the workload writes beneath it (claude-code's ~/.claude,
# npm's ~/.npm) is EACCES unless the uid owns it. So rather than
# assuming /home/cage, the tail reads field 6 back out of /etc/passwd —
# whichever branch wrote it — and makes that path exist and belong to
# 1000. No chmod: useradd and adduser each pick a sane mode, and
# forcing one here would widen a base whose login.defs chose 0750.
# An empty field 6 fails the RUN on purpose; none of the three branches
# can produce one, so it would mean /etc/passwd was not what we wrote.
RUN if ! getent passwd 1000 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && ! grep -q '^[^:]*:[^:]*:1000:' /etc/passwd; then \
        if command -v useradd >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
            useradd --uid 1000 --create-home --shell /bin/sh cage; \
        elif command -v adduser >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
            adduser -u 1000 -h /home/cage -s /bin/sh -D cage; \
        else \
            printf 'cage:x:1000:1000::/home/cage:/bin/sh\n' >>/etc/passwd \
            && printf 'cage:x:1000:\n' >>/etc/group; \
        fi \
        && cage_home=$(grep '^[^:]*:[^:]*:1000:' /etc/passwd | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f6) \
        && [ -n "${cage_home}" ] \
        && mkdir -p "${cage_home}" \
        && chown 1000:1000 "${cage_home}"; \
    fi

# Bake the user's original argv as a shell-escaped one-shot script.
# cage-init.sh exec's this after capsh-dropping. The shlex.quote on the
# Python side handles every metacharacter (spaces, $VAR, &&, ; etc.) so
# the resulting `exec ...` line is safe to feed straight to /bin/sh
# without further parsing. Closes the I2 argv-injection risk from the
# eng review on the prior runtime-jq approach.
RUN mkdir -p /opt/agentcage /etc/agentcage
RUN cat > /opt/agentcage/cage-cmd.sh <<'CAGECMD'
#!/bin/sh
exec /entrypoint.sh ''
CAGECMD
RUN chmod 0755 /opt/agentcage/cage-cmd.sh

# cage-init.sh staged into the build context by stage_build_context
# (copies from src/agentcage/data/apple-container/cage-init.sh).
COPY cage-init.sh /opt/agentcage/cage-init.sh
RUN chmod 0755 /opt/agentcage/cage-init.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/agentcage/cage-init.sh"]
CMD []
